findings.text: There is no guard against `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype` keys. For the FormData key `__proto__[polluted]`, `target['__proto__']` is Object.prototype, which is truthy and an object. buildPath therefore recurses into it and sets `polluted` on Object.prototype. `constructor[prototype][x]` does the same. This is prototype pollution from attacker-controlled form field names.

`utils.hasOwnProperty` is not defined in the patch, and the grep found no other definition, so it may not exist in `../utils`. If it is missing, every last-segment assignment throws a TypeError. Duplicate keys are also handled badly: a third value for the same key gives `[[a,b],c]` instead of `[a,b,c]`.

The path regex `\w+|\[(\w*)]` mishandles a key that is only digits and brackets, and `match[1] || match[0]` returns `[0]`-style text in some cases. An empty `[]` segment inside a non-array target gives the key '' and overwrites it. Example: `a[][b]` after `a=1`.

0.reason: Nothing filters `__proto__`. For the key `__proto__[polluted]`, `target['__proto__']` is Object.prototype, which is truthy and passes `utils.isObject`, so buildPath recurses into it and writes `polluted` onto Object.prototype. This is prototype pollution, a separate defect from the regex splitting bug.

1.reason: Whether `utils.hasOwnProperty` exists can't be checked because utils isn't provided, but line 43 does `target[name] = [target[name], value]` without checking for an existing array, so a third duplicate key really does give `[[a,b],c]` instead of `[a,b,c]`.
